annotation.title_clean: The Civil Aviation (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020
annotation.title_en: The Civil Aviation (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Minister for Works, Transport and Communication, United Republic of Tanzania
annotation.summary_en: Tanzanian amendment to the 2018 Civil Aviation (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) Regulations. It adjusts definitions, fees and age limits, requires authorisation for carrying dangerous goods, and replaces the offences and penalties provisions with fines of at least one million shillings and up to six months' imprisonment for unsafe, unauthorised, unregistered or unidentified drone operation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines 'company' to include organisations engaged in RPAS activities.
Licence and other fees are now to be prescribed by the Authority rather than fixed in US dollars.
Minimum age in regulation 46 reduced from 21 to 18, and the 'or private' wording is deleted.

New regulation 72 makes unsafe, unauthorised or unregistered RPAS operation, and failure to display an identifier, offences punishable by a fine of at least one million shillings, imprisonment up to six months, or both.
Licences and approvals may be revoked or suspended for contraventions; regulation 72A adds a general penalty.
